The University of Waterloo offers many types of credentials, with a variety of intended audiences. For example:

  • Minors are normally open to all undergraduate students.
  • Options are normally open to all students registered in a major in the same faculty as the option.
  • Specializations are normally open to all students majoring in the affiliated field.

Certain credential combinations are not permitted [Note: The following are not listed in the Specific Invalid Credential Combinations table].

  • No student may enrol in or graduate from two credentials with significant overlapping content, including, but not limited to:
    • a minor, option, or diploma/certificate in the same subject as their major (e.g., Honours Anthropology and Anthropology Minor; Honours Software Engineering and Software Engineering Option);
    • a minor and a diploma in the same subject (e.g., Church Music and Worship Minor and Diploma in Church Music and Worship);
    • more than one diploma in the same language (e.g., Diploma in Japanese Language I and Diploma in Japanese Language II);
    • the same credential that has been renamed (e.g., Communication Studies, formerly Speech Communication, language certificate that became a diploma).

To facilitate the application to graduate process, students should declare all minors, options, and specializations as early as possible, but no later than the start of their last academic term.

Additional Constraints

Faculty of Arts

  • No student may enrol in or graduate from:
    • Two intensive specializations offered by the same major.
    • Multiple “topic” specializations offered by the same major in the following majors:
      • Communication Studies (maximum of one topic specialization)
      • Economics (maximum of one topic specialization)
      • History (maximum of one topic specialization)
      • Mathematical Economics, BA (maximum of one topic specialization)
      • Theatre and Performance (maximum of one topic specialization)
    • Any two "and Financial Management" bachelor's degrees.
  • When pursuing a Bachelor of Arts, students may combine two honours major academic plans only (i.e., not an honours major plan with a general major academic plan).

Faculty of Engineering

  • No Bachelor of Architectural Studies student may enrol in or graduate from options offered by the Faculty of Engineering, except for those that explicitly allow it.

Faculty of Mathematics

  • No student may enrol in or graduate from:
    • A stand-alone Bachelor of Computer Science (BCS) academic plan with any Bachelor of Mathematics (BMath) academic plan (including Joint Honours academic plans).
    • A stand-alone BMath Joint Honours academic plan with any non-Mathematics Joint Honours academic plan.
    • Data Science (BMath or BCS) with any other Faculty of Mathematics Honours or Joint Honours academic plan, except that the BCS (Data Science) can make up the BCS component of the Business Administration and Computer Science double degree program.
    • A stand-alone BCS Honours co-operative academic plan or BMath Honours co-operative academic plan with any stand-alone regular Honours academic plan (including Joint Honours academic plans).

Faculty of Science

  • No Bachelor of Medical Sciences student may enrol in or graduate from any minor or any option offered by the Faculty of Science.

Specific Invalid Credential Combinations

The University will amend the list of invalid credential combinations when new academic programs or plans (i.e., majors, minors, options, diplomas, certificates, and specializations) are created. The University has done its best to include all specific invalid credential combinations in the table below; however, students should confirm any plan combination with their academic advisor.

Legend

* Indicates an inactivated academic program or plan. When credentials are inactivated, they will remain in this table for three years; once removed, the combination remains invalid and students should refer to historical versions of the academic calendar.
